watchlist.thesis: Oklo continues to rack up genuine regulatory and operational milestones — DOE startup authorization for the Groves test reactor (Aug 25), the March Aurora Powerhouse safety design approval, and first-ever quarterly revenue — but the stock remains rangebound in the high-$30s to low-$40s, roughly flat over the past month (-2.6%) and still well off its prior highs. There is still zero open-market insider buying (only RSU vesting and sell-to-cover tax transactions), and institutional activity remains scattered rather than a coordinated accumulation wave. Analysts continue trimming near-term price targets even while staying structurally constructive. Nothing here changes the picture materially from the prior write-up — still a well-covered story stock without the insider/technical confirmation this screen looks for.
watchlist.risks: Company remains pre-revenue at scale (Q2 revenue just $1.21M) with a wide EPS loss, so the case rests entirely on multi-year execution; heavy insider selling (all RSU/tax-driven, no buys) and continued analyst target cuts add to near-term downside risk despite the constructive long-term consensus.
